---
title: "CAS PCPA Practice Project"
subtitle: "Feature Generation"
---


## Overview

In this video we perform feature generation. We test raw vs binned forms,
polynomial terms, and interaction effects identified during EDA. Each
test compares AIC via AICtweedie and we retain whichever form produces
the lower AIC. 

---

1. Load Libraries

Load tidyverse, statmod, and tweedie for modeling
```{r}
# install.packages("tidyverse")
# install.packages("statmod")
# install.packages("tweedie")
library(tidyverse)
library(statmod)
library(tweedie)
```

---

2. Load the Data and Selected Model

Read the training set, Tweedie p, and the selected model into R
```{r}
train         <- read_csv("train_modela.csv")
p             <- readRDS("tweedie_p.rds")
model_selected <- readRDS("model_C.rds")

cat("Using Tweedie p:", round(p, 4), "\n")
cat("Selected Model AIC:", round(AICtweedie(model_C), 2), "\n")
```

---

3. Review the Selected Model Formula

Print the formula of the selected model - Model C
```{r}
formula(model_C)
```

---

4. Re-apply Factor Levels

Re-apply factor levels and reference levels since they are not
preserved when saving to CSV
```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    gender            = factor(gender),
    marital_status    = factor(marital_status),
    coverage_type     = factor(coverage_type),
    deductible        = factor(deductible),
    make              = factor(make),
    body_type         = factor(body_type),
    vehicle_use       = factor(vehicle_use),
    num_cylinders     = factor(num_cylinders),
    anti_theft_device = factor(anti_theft_device),
    safety_rating     = factor(safety_rating),
    region            = factor(region),
    urban_rural       = factor(urban_rural),
    tort_environment  = factor(tort_environment),
    catastrophe_risk  = factor(catastrophe_risk)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    gender            = relevel(gender, ref = "F"),
    marital_status    = relevel(marital_status, ref = "Married"),
    coverage_type     = relevel(coverage_type, ref = "Liability Only"),
    deductible        = relevel(deductible, ref = "500"),
    make              = relevel(make, ref = "Toyota"),
    body_type         = relevel(body_type, ref = "Sedan"),
    vehicle_use       = relevel(vehicle_use, ref = "Pleasure"),
    safety_rating     = relevel(safety_rating, ref = "3"),
    urban_rural       = relevel(urban_rural, ref = "Suburban"),
    tort_environment  = relevel(tort_environment, ref = "Moderate"),
    catastrophe_risk  = relevel(catastrophe_risk, ref = "Medium")
  )
```

Add binned versions of continuous variables for testing
```{r}
miles_breaks  <- c(0, 5000, 10000, 15000, 20000, 30000, Inf)
miles_labels  <- c("0-5k", "5k-10k", "10k-15k", "15k-20k", "20k-30k", "30k+")
value_breaks  <- c(0, 10000, 20000, 35000, 50000, Inf)
value_labels  <- c("0-10k", "10k-20k", "20k-35k", "35k-50k", "50k+")

train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    miles_band = factor(cut(annual_miles, breaks = miles_breaks, labels = miles_labels, include.lowest = TRUE),
                        levels = miles_labels),
    value_band = factor(cut(vehicle_value, breaks = value_breaks, labels = value_labels, include.lowest = TRUE),
                        levels = value_labels)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    miles_band = relevel(miles_band, ref = "10k-15k"),
    value_band = relevel(value_band, ref = "10k-20k")
  )
```

---

5. Helper Function

Create a reusable function to compare two model formulas by AIC
```{r}
compare_aic <- function(formula_1, formula_2, label_1, label_2, data, p) {
  m1 <- glm(as.formula(paste(formula_1, collapse = " ")), 
            data = data, family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0))
  m2 <- glm(as.formula(paste(formula_2, collapse = " ")), 
            data = data, family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0))
  data.frame(
    model     = c(label_1, label_2),
    AIC       = round(c(AICtweedie(m1), AICtweedie(m2)), 2),
    preferred = c(ifelse(AICtweedie(m1) < AICtweedie(m2), "YES", ""),
                  ifelse(AICtweedie(m2) < AICtweedie(m1), "YES", ""))
  )
}
```

---

6. Define the Base Formula

Define the selected model formula as a string to use as the base for
all tests.
```{r}
base_formula <- "total_losses ~ credit_score + gender + prior_claims_3yr + violations_3yr + 
    coverage_type + annual_miles + vehicle_value + vehicle_age + 
    urban_rural + tort_environment + catastrophe_risk + offset(log(exposure))"
```

---

7. Step 1 - Raw vs Binned Variable Forms

Test each continuous predictor that survived variable selection against
its binned version. We retain whichever form produces lower AIC.

7.1 Annual Miles vs Miles Band

```{r}
train %>%
  mutate(miles_band_viz = cut(annual_miles,
                              breaks = c(0, 5000, 10000, 15000, 20000, 30000, Inf),
                              labels = c("0-5k","5k-10k","10k-15k","15k-20k","20k-30k","30k+"),
                              include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(miles_band_viz) %>%
  summarize(mean_pp = mean(pure_premium)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = miles_band_viz, y = mean_pp)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Mean Pure Premium by Annual Miles",
       x = "Annual Miles Band", y = "Mean Pure Premium ($)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Test raw annual_miles against miles_band
```{r}
compare_aic(
  base_formula,
  gsub("annual_miles", "miles_band", base_formula),
  "Raw: annual_miles",
  "Binned: miles_band",
  train, p
)
```

7.3 Vehicle Value vs Value Band

```{r}
train %>%
  mutate(value_band_viz = cut(vehicle_value,
                              breaks = c(0, 10000, 20000, 35000, 50000, Inf),
                              labels = c("0-10k","10k-20k","20k-35k","35k-50k","50k+"),
                              include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(value_band_viz) %>%
  summarize(mean_pp = mean(pure_premium)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value_band_viz, y = mean_pp)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Mean Pure Premium by Vehicle Value",
       x = "Vehicle Value Band", y = "Mean Pure Premium ($)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Test raw vehicle_value against value_band
```{r}
compare_aic(
  base_formula,
  gsub("vehicle_value", "value_band", base_formula),
  "Raw: vehicle_value",
  "Binned: value_band",
  train, p
)
```

7.4 Update Base Formula with Best Forms

Update the formula to use the preferred form for each variable based
on the AIC comparisons above
```{r}
best_formula <- "total_losses ~ credit_score + gender + prior_claims_3yr + violations_3yr + coverage_type + annual_miles + value_band + vehicle_age + urban_rural + tort_environment + catastrophe_risk + offset(log(exposure))"
best_formula
```

---

8. Step 2 - Polynomial Terms

Test whether adding a quadratic term for age improves model fit. EDA
showed a U-shaped relationship between age and pure premium, and age
was not significant as a linear term during variable selection. This
is a strong candidate for a quadratic term.

8.1 Age Squared

Test linear age vs age plus age squared
```{r}
formula_age_sq <- paste0(best_formula, " + age + I(age^2)")

compare_aic(
  best_formula,
  formula_age_sq,
  "Without age",
  "With age + I(age^2)",
  train, p
)
```

Update best formula if quadratic age is preferred
```{r}
best_formula <- formula_age_sq
best_formula
```

---

9. Step 3 - Interaction Terms

Test interaction terms identified during bivariate analysis in Video 12.

9.1 Age x Gender Interaction

EDA showed young male drivers have materially higher pure premiums
than young female drivers. Test whether adding this interaction improves fit.

```{r}
train %>%
  filter(gender %in% c("M", "F")) %>%
  mutate(age_band_viz = cut(age,
                            breaks = c(15, 25, 35, 50, 65, 100),
                            labels = c("16-25","26-35","36-50","51-65","66+"),
                            include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(age_band_viz, gender) %>%
  summarize(mean_pp = mean(pure_premium), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_band_viz, y = mean_pp, color = gender, group = gender)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Mean Pure Premium by Age Band and Gender",
       subtitle = "Young males have materially higher pure premiums",
       x = "Age Band", y = "Mean Pure Premium ($)", color = "Gender") +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
formula_age_gender <- paste0(best_formula, " + age:gender")

compare_aic(
  best_formula,
  formula_age_gender,
  "Without age:gender",
  "With age:gender",
  train, p
)
```

9.2 Vehicle Use x Annual Miles Interaction

EDA showed business drivers with high mileage have the highest pure
premiums. Test whether this interaction improves fit.

```{r}
train %>%
  mutate(miles_band_viz = cut(annual_miles,
                              breaks = c(0, 10000, 15000, 20000, Inf),
                              labels = c("Low (<10k)","Medium (10-15k)",
                                         "High (15-20k)","Very High (20k+)"),
                              include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(vehicle_use, miles_band_viz) %>%
  summarize(mean_pp = mean(pure_premium), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = miles_band_viz, y = mean_pp, color = vehicle_use, group = vehicle_use)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Mean Pure Premium by Annual Miles and Vehicle Use",
       subtitle = "Business drivers show steeper increase with miles",
       x = "Annual Miles Band", y = "Mean Pure Premium ($)", color = "Vehicle Use") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```


```{r}
formula_use_miles <- paste0(best_formula, " + vehicle_use:annual_miles")

compare_aic(
  best_formula,
  formula_use_miles,
  "Without vehicle_use:annual_miles",
  "With vehicle_use:annual_miles",
  train, p
)
```

---

10. Fit the Refined Model

Fit the final refined model using the best formula after all tests
```{r}
model_D <- glm(
  as.formula(best_formula),
  data   = train,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0)
)
```

Review the refined model summary
```{r}
summary(model_D)
```

Compare AIC across all models
```{r}
cat("Model_C: ", round(AICtweedie(model_C), 2), "\n")
cat("Model_D:             ", round(AICtweedie(model_D), 2), "\n")
cat("% Deviance Explained:          ", round((1 - model_D$deviance / model_D$null.deviance) * 100, 2), "%\n")
```

---

11. Save the Refined Model

Save the refined model for use in subsequent scripts
```{r}
saveRDS(model_D, "model_D.rds") 
write_csv(train, "train_modeld.csv")
cat("Refined model saved to model_D.rds\n")
```

---

## Key Observations

- Feature engineering was performed only on variables that survived variable selection
- a more efficient and practical approach than engineering features for variables that may be dropped
- Raw vs binned forms were tested for continuous predictors using AICtweedie as the selection criterion
- A quadratic term for age was tested since age was not significant as a linear term but EDA showed a clear U-shaped relationship - this is an important teaching moment about why a variable might appear non-significant in its raw form
- Two interaction terms were tested based on EDA findings - age x gender and vehicle_use x annual_miles
- Each feature was tested individually to isolate its contribution before updating the base formula
- The refined model is carried forward into Video 18 where we perform iterative model refinement and diagnostics
